papers.title: MAHA-z: A Mahalanobis distance kNN estimator for photometric redshifts
papers.micro: On Euclid Flagship 2 (LSST+NISP) we achieve σ_NMAD=0.0148 with a 0.27% outlier fraction…
papers.abstract: We present MAHA-z, a photometric-redshift (photo-z) estimator that combines k-nearest neighbour (kNN) regression with a Mahalanobis distance metric learned from the covariance of a spectroscopic reference sample. For each target galaxy, MAHA-z performs a neighbour search in a colour-magnitude feature space with optional morphological parameters, and returns both a point estimate and a redshift posterior p(zmidf) obtained by kernel density estimation over the neighbour redshifts. The Mahalanobis metric accounts for correlated features and heterogeneous units, eliminating ad hoc normalisation, and its subspace restriction allows MAHA-z to handle missing bands on a per-galaxy basis without imputation. We validate the method on four datasets spanning simulations and survey photometry: the Euclid Flagship 2 mock, the Legacy-KiDZ calibration sample, VIPERS, and the DES Year 3 BAO sample. On Euclid Flagship 2 (LSST+NISP) we achieve σ_NMAD=0.0148 with a 0.27% outlier fraction, and on DES Y3 we obtain σ_NMAD≈0.023 with <1% outliers and posterior calibration comparable to the ANNz2 catalogue. MAHA-z processes millions of galaxies in minutes and provides competitive PDFs at substantially lower computational cost than trained machine-learning models, making it a practical option for iterative photo-z production and validation in Stage-IV surveys.

papers.title: A Positive Turn: Coupled Quintessence and Cosmological Neutrino Masses
papers.micro: Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within 2σ for normal…
papers.abstract: In ΛCDM, the CMB and DESI BAO upper limits on the total neutrino mass are in tension with the lower bounds from oscillation experiments, and analyses allowing negative effective masses favor negative values. We investigate whether a coupled quintessence (CQ) model in which dark matter interacts with a canonical scalar field φ through an exponential mass coupling mc(φ)∝ e^(−βφ/MPl) can alleviate this tension. Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within 2σ for normal ordering, without requiring the scalar-field equation of state to cross the phantom divide. We further show that it alleviates the tension more effectively than alternative interacting dark energy models that instead favor more negative effective masses. This comparison shows that whether dark sector interactions can relax neutrino mass bounds ultimately depends on the interplay of their effects on primary CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables

papers.title: galpy with differentiable, accelerated backends: galactic dynamics in jax and PyTorch
papers.micro: To illustrate the new capabilities, we present simple examples of fitting the Galactic potential with a hypervelocity star and of learning the inverse action-angle transformation with a neural…
papers.abstract: We describe an extension of galpy, the Python library for galactic dynamics, that adds jax and PyTorch as computational backends alongside its existing numpy and C implementation. With it, galpy's gravitational potentials, orbit integration, action-angle transformations and their inverses, and distribution functions, including those for tidal streams, run on GPUs, can be compiled as part of a user's program, and can be differentiated with respect to their inputs and parameters, from the force at a point to the samples drawn from a distribution function. The user-facing design is kept simple: the active backend follows from the type of the arrays that are passed in, the galpy interface is unchanged, and the numpy path gives the same results as before. We describe the design of the backend framework and its implementation in each of galpy's modules, with examples of use, and we discuss its limitations. On a GPU, batches of orbits, samples from distribution functions, and stream models run one to five orders of magnitude faster than on a single CPU core. To illustrate the new capabilities, we present simple examples of fitting the Galactic potential with a hypervelocity star and of learning the inverse action-angle transformation with a neural network trained through galpy. An AI coding agent wrote essentially all of the code under the detailed direction and review of the human author, and we describe how we organized this work and how we established the correctness of the result. This work is the start of galpy's version 2, which is available at https://github.com/jobovy/galpy and documented at https://docs.galpy.org/en/v2/.

papers.title: ViViViT: a Video-to-Video Vision Transformer for Cosmological Lightcone Reconstruction
papers.micro: By encoding the evolving geometry of the cosmological observable itself…
papers.abstract: Moving along the line of sight of a cosmological lightcone also moves through cosmic time, as in a video of cosmic structure traced by an evolving observable. We recast the reconstruction of the underlying matter field from observed lightcones as a video-to-video translation task by introducing ViViViT, a vision transformer that factorizes attention across transverse frames and radial evolution. On reconstructed matter fields from 21cm neutral hydrogen simulations over z∈[7.66,16.00], ViViViT preserves spectral power and phase alignment within a few percent of the ground truth up to the Nyquist scale, and three-point correlations for all triangle configurations with sides up to k≃0.77 h/Mpc, outperforming a convolutional 3D-U-Net baseline across all measured statistics. By encoding the evolving geometry of the cosmological observable itself, ViViViT marks a step toward field-level architectures that natively respect cosmic time, opening the path to time-aware reconstruction of cosmic tracers and targeted searches for redshift-dependent signatures in 21cm data.

papers.title: Early-Excess SNe Ia Show Strong C II Absorption
papers.micro: Early-excess objects (n=13) tend to exhibit stronger C II absorption than non-excesses (n=22) at phases earlier than approximately −13 d…
papers.abstract: Some type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit an early excess in their rising light curves, but the physical origin of this behavior remains uncertain. The processes driving these excesses affect the ejecta at early times and may also imprint on the outermost layers. We investigate whether early excesses are associated with differences in unburned material by measuring pre-maximum carbon absorption. Using multi-component Gaussian fits to the blended Si II λ6355 and C II λ6580 region, we measure pseudo-equivalent widths and velocities for a sample of 35 nonpeculiar SNe Ia with rising light curve categorizations. We find that early-excess objects (n=13) tend to exhibit stronger C II absorption than non-excesses (n=22) at phases earlier than approximately −13 d, with a two-sample K-S test of the earliest measurements yielding p=0.025. In contrast, the HV Si II components do not clearly separate the two groups. Early-excess SNe Ia tend to be more luminous and decline more slowly, but objects with similar maximum-light properties span a range of C II pseudo-equivalent widths, suggesting that this effect is distinct from the known luminosity-width relation. We show that, at least in some cases, when objects have similar light-curve shape and photospheric temperature, the effect we see is not driven by ionization but by distinct differences in the explosion, such as carbon abundance and density and the efficiency of burning in the WD. Our results provide a new constraint on SN Ia explosion models for early excesses, as they must produce a tendency for stronger early C II absorption.

papers.title: Robustness of the Baryonic Acoustic Oscillation Peak Position against Monopole Fluctuations in Galaxy Surveys
papers.micro: Our results demonstrate the robustness of the BAO analysis against the unknown systematic error.
papers.abstract: Precise measurements of the baryonic acoustic oscillation (BAO) peak position are one of the key goals in modern galaxy surveys. We investigate the impact of the monopole fluctuations in galaxy surveys on the BAO peak position in the galaxy two-point redshift-space multipole-correlation functions. The background mean density of a galaxy sample is estimated from the survey itself by averaging the observed galaxy number density, and this averaged number density (monopole) is subtracted to obtain the observed galaxy number density fluctuation, which includes an additional contribution from the monopole fluctuations, propagating to galaxy clustering analysis. We compute the contributions of the monopole fluctuations to the redshift-space multipole-correlation functions. While the monopole contributions in galaxy two-point correlation function are anisotropic and non-negligible in amplitude, the contributions are so smooth around the BAO peak position that they are almost completely absorbed in the BAO broadband model, leaving the BAO peak position unaffected at the sub-percent level. Our results demonstrate the robustness of the BAO analysis against the unknown systematic error.

papers.title: Type Ia-CSM Supernovae. I. Uniform Light-Curve Characterization and Inference on the Underlying Type Ia Explosions
papers.micro: Subsequent papers in this series will utilize numerical simulations, semi-analytical modeling, spectroscopy, and host-galaxy environments to further constrain the progenitor and explosion pathways to SNe Ia-CSM.
papers.abstract: We present the largest uniform study to date of 50 thermonuclear Type Ia supernovae interacting with circumstellar medium (SNe Ia-CSM). As the first paper in a series delineating the population properties of this class, this work focuses specifically on a uniform analysis of their light curves. Our results show that SNe Ia-CSM display a significantly more uniform light-curve morphology than interacting core-collapse SNe IIn, closely resembling the luminous-slow subgroup. The Ia-CSM sample spans approximately an order of magnitude in peak luminosity, total timescale, and radiated energy, with a median optical peak luminosity of ≈2×10⁴³ erg s⁻¹ (≈−20 mag). We find a distinct bimodality in the radiated energy distribution: a predominant population of energetic events with ≈ 2×10⁵⁰ erg and characteristic timescales of ≈100 days, and a secondary population that is roughly an order of magnitude less energetic with shorter timescales of ≈50 days. Decomposition of the luminosity contributions from underlying SN Ia and CSM interaction by the Ia-CSM spectral classification reveals a diverse range of underlying SN Ia subtypes spanning from luminous 1991T-like to faint 1991bg-like. Both SN Ia and CSM properties are broadly consistent with the core-degenerate channel resulting from common-envelope evolution followed by core merger, where the presence of dense CSM is dictated by the delay time between the common-envelope phase and the thermonuclear explosion. Subsequent papers in this series will utilize numerical simulations, semi-analytical modeling, spectroscopy, and host-galaxy environments to further constrain the progenitor and explosion pathways to SNe Ia-CSM.

papers.title: A self-shadowing black hole accretion disk at sub-Eddington luminosities
papers.micro: Observations of similar systems suggest that this phenomenon may be common among black hole accretion disks.
papers.abstract: Accretion onto black holes powers some of the most energetic sources in the Universe, yet its behaviour across the luminosity range remains poorly understood. Specifically, as the luminosity approaches the Eddington limit (LEdd), the inner accretion disk is expected to depart from the standard thin-disk solution, becoming vertically extended. The luminosity threshold and observational signatures of this transition remain, however, uncertain. We present multiwavelength spectroscopy obtained during the decay of a black hole X-ray binary outburst. At the peak (∼ 0.2 LEdd), a cool optical and near-infrared spectrum dominated by strong recombination lines of hydrogen and He I is observed. However, as the luminosity decreases, it switches to a hot, highly irradiated, nearly featureless spectrum. This puzzling behavior reveals the emergence of a vertically extended inner disk at the outburst peak, shielding the outer regions from high-energy radiation produced near the black hole; a scenario supported by contemporaneous X-ray spectra. Observations of similar systems suggest that this phenomenon may be common among black hole accretion disks. Self-shadowing structures at luminosities well below LEdd have major implications for black hole accretion flows and their observational properties, affecting inferred black hole spins, X-ray polarization measurements, and the physical conditions of the outer disk and its associated outflows.

papers.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
papers.micro: Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime.
papers.abstract: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.

papers.title: Beyond classification: regressing physical merger properties using solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum
papers.micro: Most importantly, we show that for the first time this method is able to regress on both merger mass ratio and time since merger simultaneously…
papers.abstract: Galaxy mergers play an important role in galaxy evolution; they enhance star formation, transform morphologies, and may drive accretion onto black holes. Due to their complex morphological features, identification of mergers poses a significant challenge. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been successful at identifying mergers with good accuracy. However, similar to other deep learning techniques such as Vision Transformers, they require large training samples. Current methods are also limited to classification, rather than regression. Here, we apply the solid harmonic wavelet scattering bispectrum, a method that encodes invariances and symmetries in the data which need to be learned by CNNs, as an alternative to CNNs. We apply our methodology to a simulated dataset of galaxies with a wide range of merger properties. We show that this method outperforms standard methodologies, while requiring fewer training samples and being robust to noise. Most importantly, we show that for the first time this method is able to regress on both merger mass ratio and time since merger simultaneously, with uncertainties   0.33 dex uncertainty in merger mass ratio and   0.66 Gyr uncertainty in time since merger. We have therefore shown that solid harmonic wavelet bispectrum presents an alternative to currently used machine learning techniques.

papers.title: Observational constraints on CO sequestration and disk mass in the planet-hosting PDS 70 disk
papers.micro: The derived disk mass drops by a factor of ∼ 3.4 from 0.039^+0.067_−0.018 M☉ to 0.011^+0.011_−0.006 M☉ if the C¹⁷O line flux is included in the fitting procedure…
papers.abstract: Exoplanets accrete gas, dust, and ice from their natal environment, setting the chemical composition of their atmospheres and interiors. The abundance of the major volatiles in disks can be used to possibly link exoplanet atmospheres to their formation location in the disk. In this work, we aim to quantify the peak CO abundance and disk mass of the PDS 70 disk, the first disk with a direct confirmation of two accreting planets in its dust cavity. We present the first detection of N₂H⁺ and C¹⁷O in this disk. The C¹⁷O emission shows marginal statistical evidence for an azimuthal asymmetry trailing that previously seen in the continuum emission. We then compare the disk integrated fluxes of N₂H⁺, CO isotopologues, and the continuum to an existing grid of thermochemical models. We find that the derived disk mass drops by a factor of ∼ 3.4 from 0.039^+0.067_−0.018 M☉ to 0.011^+0.011_−0.006 M☉ if the C¹⁷O line flux is included in the fitting procedure; the quoted intervals do not include systematic uncertainties. CO on the other hand is sequestered with an effective abundance of (4.8^+4.3_−2.7 − 17⁺⁸₋₈) × 10⁻⁶ relative to H₂ in the probed disk layers after accounting for CO freeze-out and isotope selective CO photodissociation for the adopted chemical network and ionization prescription. The range in peak CO abundances reflects the uncertainty in the N₂H⁺ emission, assuming either optically thin emission at 21 K or optically thick emission. Therefore, the PDS 70 planets are possibly accreting the final portion of their atmospheres from the outer disk molecular layer where CO is sequestered. Thus, CO sequestering may need to be considered when interpreting the chemical composition of planetary atmospheres.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in A&A

papers.title: FRIDA: Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies. I. Programme overview, resolved gas density profiles, and HI mass-size relation
papers.micro: ΣHI(R/RHI) and MHI(<R)/MHI for UDGs follow an intermediate trend between late-type discs and early-type galaxies, with a large overlap with Sa galaxies.
papers.abstract: Gas-rich ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) provide powerful tests of galaxy formation models at low surface densities. However, the structure of their neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) remains poorly constrained, hampering our understanding of this population. We present FRIDA (Finding Rotation In ultra-Diffuse gAlaxies), a MeerKAT and VLA programme providing high-resolution HI data of 12 gas-rich UDGs. In this paper, we introduce our sample and delve into the associated observations and data reduction. We derive HI fluxes, masses (MHI), and resolved surface density profiles (ΣHI(R)). We find extended (∼ 7−30 kpc in radius) and regular HI emission in our UDGs, and we report the discovery of a satellite around one of them. Most UDGs in FRIDA have ΣHI(R) profiles with flat inner parts reaching ΣHI(R)≈ 4 M☉ pc⁻² near their centres, which then decline exponentially in their outer parts. By modelling the HI morphology of the UDGs, we find a median inclination of 43°, in agreement with theoretical expectations for disc galaxies under UDG selection effects. Moreover, we place our UDGs in the MHI−RHI and MHI−R_50,HI mass-size relations, where RHI is radius at which ΣHI(R)=1 M☉ pc⁻², and R_50,HI is the radius enclosing 50% of MHI. While our UDGs lie within the scatter of the relations, they systematically fall on their upper side, being slightly (by ∼ 15−25%) more extended and of lower mean ΣHI (by ∼ 25−35%) than average galaxies at similar MHI. Moreover, we find that ΣHI(R/RHI) and MHI(<R)/MHI for UDGs follow an intermediate trend between late-type discs and early-type galaxies, with a large overlap with Sa galaxies.

papers.title: Dark matter alters dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies
papers.micro: By comparing the same systems across cold dark matter and varied self-interacting dark matter models…
papers.abstract: Dwarf galaxies are the most dark-matter-dominated systems in the Universe, serving as unique laboratories for exploring the fundamental nature of the dark sector. Although the observed diversity in dwarf galaxy sizes and morphologies suggests an interplay between dark matter and baryonic physics, this relationship has remained largely unquantified in existing models. Here, we utilize a set of novel cosmological simulations with baryons to demonstrate how dark matter physics directly drives the structural evolution of these galaxies. By comparing the same systems across cold dark matter and varied self-interacting dark matter models, we find that the evolution of the central density of dark matter significantly impacts a galaxy's half-light radius, but the signal is dependent on morphology. This causal link establishes galaxy size as a direct signature of the underlying dark matter microphysics. Our findings provide a predictive framework for decoding dark matter particle properties from galactic shapes, offering a roadmap for upcoming wide-field surveys, such as the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, to probe the dark sector through the statistical analysis of galaxy populations.

papers.title: Variations in the Extinction Curve at High Galactic Latitudes as seen by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument
papers.micro: We find no strong relationship between R(V) and other tracers of the interstellar medium, such as thermal emission, dust temperature, spectral emissivity index β, and Hα.
papers.abstract: The dust extinction curve, characterized by the total-to-selective extinction ratio, R(V), varies with grain size and composition. Accurate R(V) values are crucial for dereddening astronomical colors and understanding the interstellar medium. We measure extinction toward stars with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy using a machine-learning-based relative of the "pair method," matching reddened and unreddened stars. We use XGBoost to predict stars' intrinsic colors from their spectroscopic parameters (Teff, log g, [Fe/H]) and subtract them from observed colors to measure reddening in combinations of the g, r, z, W1, and W2 bands. This approach directly measures reddening, unlike the common thermal-emission-based method of Schlegel et al. (1998; SFD). The reddening is accurate to roughly 0.02 mag in g−r and r−z. We develop a forward model to map g−r and g−W1 reddenings to R(V) and find significant variation in R(V), with σ_NMAD(R(V)) = 0.23, in dusty regions (E(g−r) > 0.1) at high Galactic latitudes observed by DESI. In this footprint, R(V) is bimodal, with modes at 2.9 and 3.4, likely due to large-spatial-scale correlations in the shape of the extinction curve combined with the relatively small number of distinct sightlines with substantial reddening. We find no strong relationship between R(V) and other tracers of the interstellar medium, such as thermal emission, dust temperature, spectral emissivity index β, and Hα. However, the error in the SFD-predicted extinction correlates well with R(V), implying that a single optical reddening combined with the far-infrared dust brightness can predict variations in the extinction curve.

papers.title: Tracing Galactic Dust Reddening with Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Emission: SPHEREx Observations of the North Ecliptic Pole
papers.micro: Applying a spectral template-based method to SPHEREx data, we measure the strength of the 3.3 μm PAH feature in each 6”.2 pixel of a 22° by 22° region…
papers.abstract: We investigate the ability of SPHEREx observations of the 3.3 μm polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission feature to trace Galactic dust reddening. Applying a spectral template-based method to SPHEREx data, we measure the strength of the 3.3 μm PAH feature in each 6”.2 pixel of a 22° by 22° region centered on the north ecliptic pole (NEP). We convert the PAH feature strength to reddening by applying a radiation field correction and a linear scale factor. The resulting E(B−V) map is consistent with far-infrared, stellar, and HI-based reddening maps at arcminute scales, exhibiting a typical E(B−V) difference of ≲ 7 mmag. A galaxy count test finds that all reddening maps have a dispersion of ≈11 mmag in E(B−V) relative to what would be needed to produce spatially uniform galaxy counts. While there is some evidence that reddening is overestimated by our map at high PAH abundances, this effect is smaller than the uncertainties on the applied radiation field corrections and limited to ∼10 mmag in the most extreme regions of the NEP. For a diffuse, high Galactic latitude region like the NEP and at the sensitivities of our validation metrics, the SPHEREx PAH-emission based reddening map matches the accuracy of existing reddening maps while being capable of accessing a higher angular resolution of ∼6”.

papers.title: Revisiting the distance to 4U 1543-475 through X-ray dust-scattering rings
papers.micro: By combining the angular radii of the rings with the independently determined distances of the scattering dust layers and the epochs of the corresponding outbursts…
papers.abstract: We derived a geometrical distance of the black-hole X-ray binary 4U 1543-475 based on X-ray dust-scattering rings associated with its 1992 and 2002 outbursts. We analyzed archival ROSAT and XMM-Newton observations and identified an X-ray dust-scattering ring in each observation, produced by two different dust layers along the line of sight. By combining the angular radii of the rings with the independently determined distances of the scattering dust layers and the epochs of the corresponding outbursts, we derive a best-constrained distance to 4U 1543-475 of 4.6 ± 0.2 kpc. This value is substantially smaller than the distance of 7.5 kpc commonly adopted in the literature and has important implications for the inferred physical properties of the system. In particular, the revised distance favors the presence of a low-mass extended-horizontal-branch donor star over a main-sequence star, calling for a reassessment of the dynamical parameters of the binary and, consequently, of the black-hole mass. The smaller distance also affects the inferred properties of the relativistic jet and the estimate of black-hole spin derived from the spectral continuum-fitting.

papers.title: Signatures of CH₄ and NH₃ in the atmosphere of β Pictoris b
papers.micro: If confirmed, these would be the first detections of both species in the atmosphere of β Pic b.
papers.abstract: β Pictoris is a nearby (19.7 pc), young (∼ 24 Myr), bright (V = 3.85) planetary system hosting three directly imaged planets. Previous high-resolution spectroscopy of β Pic b has detected H₂O and CO, but not CH₄ or NH₃. Combining observations across a broad wavelength range has been shown to maximise sensitivity to such weak molecular signals. We searched for previously undetected molecular species in the atmosphere of β Pic b using high-resolution near-infrared spectra. We combined 44 CRIRES+ spectral settings covering the H, K, L, and M bands and cross-correlated the extracted planetary spectra with molecular templates. For species with uncertain detectability, we weighted the observations by their molecular information content and data quality, independent of the measured candidate-species cross-correlation functions. We recover H₂O and CO at cross-correlation S/N values of approximately 200 and 50, respectively. We additionally identify tentative CH₄ and NH₃ signals near the expected radial velocity of β Pic b, with S/N values of approximately 5.3 and 5.7. Equivalent extractions at the same projected separation on the opposite side of the star show no comparable peaks. We classify the CH₄ and NH₃ signals as tentative because their cross-correlation S/N values do not fully account for possible residual systematics. If confirmed, these would be the first detections of both species in the atmosphere of β Pic b.

papers.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: I. Population Synthesis Framework and Illustrative Examples
papers.micro: For each system, we identify the evolutionary channel(s) that could have led to the current observational characteristics, and isolate regions of allowed natal kicks and progenitor parameter space.
papers.abstract: The natal kicks imparted to neutron stars and black holes at birth are critical for understanding massive-star evolution, compact-object formation, and compact binary merger rates. However, constraining these kicks is challenging, since they cannot be directly observed. Here, we outline a framework for inferring natal kick probability distributions for compact binaries. Our method embeds the rapid binary-population code COSMIC in a Monte-Carlo workflow that evolves ensembles of simulated binaries. From those which host compact objects, we can select subsets that match the observational characteristics of any given system (e.g. component masses, orbital period, mass-transfer status, systemic velocity). As a proof-of-concept, we apply this framework to six compact binaries spanning a wide range of companion masses and compact-object types. For each system, we identify the evolutionary channel(s) that could have led to the current observational characteristics, and isolate regions of allowed natal kicks and progenitor parameter space. We reconfirm that at least one black hole system, XTE J1118+480, must have received a natal kick vNK > 100 km s⁻¹. The neutron-star system, GX 301-2, is also inferred to have received an impulsive kick exceeding 280 km s⁻¹. We discuss the strengths and limitations associated with population-synthesis-based inference methods and explore the effects of adopting different prescriptions for critical binary evolution phases. We provide a detailed demonstration of the non-linear relationship between vNK and vsys, highlighting the shortcomings of relying on observations alone to measure natal kicks. The inferred kick velocity distributions across our benchmark sample are generally consistent with previous constraints.

papers.title: Hydrolyzed Hazes on Water-rich Exoplanets: Composition and Prebiotic Chemistry
papers.micro: The hydrolyzed samples exhibit a broader distribution in H/C and O/C ratios, and the molecular formulas suggest complex carbohydrate chemistry that challenges current theories of prebiotic organic delivery.
papers.abstract: Although photochemical hazes complicate the spectroscopic analysis of sub-Neptunes, the very presence of hazes can teach us about the habitability of these planets. Aside from affecting a planet's atmospheric and surface dynamics, hazes offer a source of organics potentially including prebiotic molecules like amino acids, nucleobases, and sugars. These organics are particularly compelling for temperate, water-rich planets where hazes may react with liquid water in condensate clouds or surface reservoirs. Hydrolysis reactions drive molecular reorganization and oxygenation, increasing the chemical complexity of the prebiotic inventory. This water-based evolution of hazes in their environment is largely unexplored and will have consequences for their chemical and optical behavior. In this work, we examine the chemical evolution of temperate water-rich exoplanet haze analogs in liquid water. High-resolution mass spectrometry finds thousands of CHNO molecules with bonding behaviors and chemical complexities distinct from the unaltered haze analogs. The oxygen weight percent increases significantly in the soluble fraction and moderately in the insoluble fraction after hydrolysis, with different carbon bonding structures demonstrating the redistribution of functional groups. The hydrolyzed samples exhibit a broader distribution in H/C and O/C ratios, and the molecular formulas suggest complex carbohydrate chemistry that challenges current theories of prebiotic organic delivery.

papers.title: On the Excitation of Sloshing Oscillations in Hot Coronal Loops
papers.micro: These results reveal the dependence of sloshing oscillation excitation on the temporal characteristics of flares.
papers.abstract: Observations of hot coronal loops have often shown the presence of compressive plasma oscillations. These oscillations are usually preceded by a flare-associated localised brightening in the vicinity of one of the footpoints of the coronal loop. The flare heating produces an impulsive injection of plasma into the coronal loop, along with a plasma perturbation that bounces back and forth between the two footpoints, termed as sloshing oscillations. While the association of these oscillations with flares is apparent, the pertinent connection between their excitation and the flare characteristics remains poorly understood. In this study, using data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) onboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we present a unique set of observations, where the response of a single coronal loop due to repeated flares in the same active region is evident. Our analysis reveals that in three out of five flare events, sloshing oscillations are triggered, while in the other two events, only plasma flows are observed. By examining the duration of plasma injection associated with each flare, we find that sloshing oscillations occur when the injection duration is shorter than the travel time of the plasma perturbation across the loop. In contrast, no oscillations are observed when the injection duration is comparable to the travel time. These results reveal the dependence of sloshing oscillation excitation on the temporal characteristics of flares.

papers.title: CosmoSim: Lens-parameter estimation of the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 using machine learning
papers.micro: We present the first application of CosmoSim to real data.
papers.abstract: CosmoSim is an open-source tool for simulating gravitational lenses and reconstructing lens mass distributions, either by ray tracing a parametric lens model or through a Roulette expansion of the lens potential. It is also used to generate the large, labelled synthetic image sets needed to train machine-learning (ML) parameter estimators. We present the first application of CosmoSim to real data. A convolutional neural network trained only on CosmoSim images estimates Singular Isothermal Ellipsoid lens and source parameters directly from observed images. We test the pipeline on 21 images of 19 strong lenses from Euclid and the AGEL survey, after removing the foreground lens light with a custom decontamination tool built on AstroPy. As a case study we reconstruct the Einstein Cross NGC 6505 both from the lens model published by the discovery team and from parameters predicted by our ML model. Both reconstructions recover the observed four-image structure, and the ML-based reconstruction performs at least as well as the literature-based one: it scores better on masked structural similarity, intersection-over-union and Chamfer distance, with an essentially equal Hausdorff distance. Across the ensemble, the predicted Einstein radii are consistent with catalogued values within the quoted uncertainties (mean relative difference 0.08 for Euclid and 0.19 for AGEL lenses), and the enclosed masses agree to within a median of 0.12 dex. The predicted ellipticities differ systematically from the catalogued values, while the comparison of orientations is inconclusive. These results establish CosmoSim as a tool that can be applied directly to observational data.

papers.title: Natal Kicks of Compact Binaries: II. Neutron-star and black-hole systems share similar kick distributions
papers.micro: Despite still being limited by small-number statistics, we find that black holes can receive large natal kicks, and that kicks for all remnant types span similar ranges (0-700 km s⁻¹).
papers.abstract: Natal kicks - kinematic impulses to neutron stars and black holes at birth - play a decisive role in the end-stage evolution of binaries hosting massive stars, in determining the global phase-space properties of compact objects, and in setting expected merger-rates detectable through gravitational-wave observations. Inferring the kick (vNK) for individual systems requires well constrained binary system properties and centre-of-mass kinematics, which must then be modelled to constrain likely system characteristics at supernova. As a result, population-wide studies of kicks remain few and far between. Here, we model plausible evolutionary histories for 68 accreting binaries, encompassing almost all black-hole and neutron-star X-ray binaries with 3D kinematics measurements, constraining allowed vNK distributions for each source using a simulation framework presented in our previous paper. The resultant vNK distribution for the sample can be simply represented by a broad Gamma distribution with mean vNK = 128⁺¹⁷₋₁₅ km s⁻¹ and scatter σ = 117 km s⁻¹. Intriguingly, the distributions for black-hole vs. neutron-star systems are found to be formally indistinguishable. Despite still being limited by small-number statistics, we find that black holes can receive large natal kicks, and that kicks for all remnant types span similar ranges (0-700 km s⁻¹). There is a hint, but no statistically significant evidence at present, for vNK scaling inversely with black-hole mass. Our work suggests either that similar physics drives kicks and shows evidence for effects beyond simplistic fallback-moderated scaling for black holes, or that selection effects conspire to erase differences between remnant types in current accreting-binary samples. Larger samples are needed to provide robust discriminatory tests between these possibilities.

papers.title: Astrometric modeling of unresolved variable binary systems
papers.micro: Both binary motion and the VIM effect can significantly impact parallax and proper motion measurements…
papers.abstract: Gaia DR4 will, for the first time, provide epoch astrometry. When analysing these data, binary sources must be treated carefully, as modelling their astrometry as single stars can bias parallax and proper motion estimates. We developed the vimbinary tool, a framework to simulate and interpret epoch astrometry of unresolved binary systems and to evaluate the impact of model assumptions on the resulting astrometric parameters. We simulated Gaia DR4-like epoch astrometry for a sample of 17 well-characterised unresolved binary systems, including both non-pulsating binaries and systems containing one photometric variable component - variability-induced movers (VIMs). We show that both binary motion and the VIM effect can significantly impact parallax and proper motion measurements, with the magnitude of the effect strongly dependent on the orbital period, photocentric amplitude, and flux ratio of the specific system. We also show that larger time coverage does not necessarily improve parallax precision, in contrast to proper motion, for which precision generally improves with longer baselines. Instead, parallaxes retrieved with binary-system fitting are more accurate than those obtained within the single-star framework.

papers.title: DIISC-VIII: Chemical Signatures of Gas Accretion in Star-Forming Galaxies
papers.micro: These results suggest that localized accretion of low-metallicity gas can sustain star formation in galaxies and demonstrate that ALM regions provide a spatially resolved indirect view of ongoing gas cycling.
papers.abstract: We investigate anomalously low-metallicity (ALM) star-forming regions in 11 galaxies from the Deciphering the Interplay between the Interstellar Medium, Stars, and the Circumgalactic Medium (DIISC) survey. We combine optical spectroscopy of 542 Hα-bright regions from MMT/Binospec with imaging from the Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope and H I 21 cm imaging from the Very Large Array. We find 75 ALM regions: 19 identified using deviations from each galaxy's radial metallicity gradient, 27 using the resolved mass–metallicity relation (rMZR), and 29 via both methods. Regions identified by both methods are metal-poor relative to their galactocentric positions and local stellar mass surface densities by > 0.1 dex, making them the strongest candidates for localized metallicity dilution. We estimate accreted masses of 5.6<log(Macc/ M☉)<7.5 for the 48 radial-gradient-selected regions, comparable to observed and simulated high-velocity cloud masses. We calculate a mean hydrogen accretion rate of 1.02 M☉ yr⁻¹ per galaxy, which is comparable to the mean star formation rate of the sample. The strongest ALM candidates lie within or near R₂₅, while rMZR-only regions dominate the outer population. We find no evidence that circumgalactic Lyα absorption along a single sightline traces disk chemical structure, as quantified by either the radial metallicity gradient or the fraction of radial-gradient-selected ALM regions. These results suggest that localized accretion of low-metallicity gas can sustain star formation in galaxies and demonstrate that ALM regions provide a spatially resolved indirect view of ongoing gas cycling.

papers.title: Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
papers.micro: These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics…
papers.abstract: We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching  280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to  3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

papers.title: MAGI (Multivariate Autoencoder for particle Generative Inference): a generative Machine Learning framework for accelerated multi-stage particle simulations
papers.micro: These first results validate MAGI v1.0.0 released on GitHub.
papers.abstract: Monte Carlo particle simulations are hindered by the computational cost of particle transport. This is especially true when large mass surrounds a small sensitive volume. MAGI is a conditional variational autoencoder that learns the joint energy, position and direction distribution of particles crossing a closed surface in a multi-stage simulation, to be resampled and re-injected in a smaller mass model. We validated it generating crossings, variables describing particle features later in the simulation, injecting them into the same Geant4 mass model and comparing the spectrum and counts at detector level with full simulation. Rates per injected crossing agree with unity at ∼1σ on our benchmark models. We measure the gain of MAGI with statistical amplification 1/χ and computational speed-up S: the first goes from 150 for high-statistics cosmic rays to 12000 for rare radioactive decays, while the latter ranges from 2.1 to almost 240, depending on source type and mass model. These first results validate MAGI v1.0.0 released on GitHub.

papers.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
papers.micro: Due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.
papers.abstract: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia 3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of P=331.52±0.02 days. Our measure of the eccentricity (e=0.9462±0.0017) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia 3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia 3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet (d ≈ 35 pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

papers.title: The Gaia-alerted 2024–2025 brightening of V346 Nor
papers.micro: With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.
papers.abstract: Young stellar objects (YSOs) build their final mass through a highly unsteady, episodic accretion process, often accompanied by outflow and ejection events. Objects undergoing episodic high-accretion states are known as eruptive YSOs. V346 Nor is an embedded eruptive YSO that underwent a sudden optical brightening in 2024 July that triggered an alert from the Gaia Photometric Science Alert system. With the aim of characterizing the physical processes behind this recent brightening event, we analyze new and archival photometric and spectroscopic monitoring data. We study how the brightness, colors, and spectral features changed with time in the past decade. We also fitted an accretion disk model to the observations in which the stellar mass–accretion rate product M⋆M and the line-of-sight extinction AV are free parameters. The accretion rate in V346 Nor has been higher (M⋆M ∼ 10⁻⁴ M☉² yr⁻¹) since 2021 than during any previous historical peak, although it was relatively constant during the 2025 February-May brightness maximum, which was driven instead by a drop in extinction from AV ≈ 20 mag to 10 mag. V346 Nor has accreted about 2% of the stellar mass since its outburst. A P Cygni profile in Hα indicates a strong outflowing wind reminiscent of classical FUors. The variability of the CaII infrared triplet lines and transient CO bandhead emission point to a highly unstable inner disk and accretion region. The persistence of forbidden line emission indicates ongoing jet activity. The brightness and color variations of V346 Nor are the result of a superposition of changes in the accretion rate and the line-of-sight extinction. With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.

papers.title: Characterization of the mechanical vibrations of the Schmidt Camera at the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory
papers.micro: Preliminary measurements reveal dominant frequency components and their corresponding amplitudes, providing insight into the telescope's dynamic behavior and potential structural couplings that may affect image quality.
papers.abstract: Mechanical vibrations in astronomical telescopes can degrade image quality, making their detection and characterization essential. This work presents the development and validation of a low-cost, portable vibration monitoring system based on MEMS accelerometers interfaced with a microcontroller. The system integrates sensor acquisition and data analysis capabilities and was evaluated through controlled laboratory tests. The system was subsequently deployed at the historic Schmidt Camera of the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory in Mexico. After more than 80 years of operation, this study represents the first characterization of its mechanical vibrations. Preliminary measurements reveal dominant frequency components and their corresponding amplitudes, providing insight into the telescope's dynamic behavior and potential structural couplings that may affect image quality. Understanding the vibrational environment of astronomical telescopes is essential for the successful integration of new instrumentation. Identifying vibration frequencies and amplitudes can support the development of mitigation strategies, data filtering techniques, and numerical simulations to predict image quality degradation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of low-cost inertial sensing for monitoring heritage-class telescopes and provide a foundation for future instrumentation and preservation efforts at the Tonantzintla Observatory.

papers.title: Origins of Satellite-System Building Blocks I: Solid Delivery During Jupiter's Growth
papers.micro: We find that, although proto-Jupiter rapidly opens a gap in the planetesimal disk, planetesimals continue to enter the CPD for more than 1 Myr.
papers.abstract: Jupiter's satellites formed within a circumplanetary disk (CPD), but the origin and delivery of the solids from which they accreted remain uncertain. Here, we investigate the delivery of planetesimal material to the CPD while consistently accounting for the growth of Jupiter and the evolution of its surrounding planetesimal reservoir. Using N-body simulations coupled to an evolving CPD model, we quantify the solid mass supplied through planetesimal ablation and direct capture. We find that, although proto-Jupiter rapidly opens a gap in the planetesimal disk, planetesimals continue to enter the CPD for more than 1 Myr. Under efficient ablation, the mass deposited in the CPD can reach approximately 1 Me, about one order of magnitude higher than the mass delivered through direct capture. However, the low efficiency of pebble accretion within the CPD implies that forming the Galilean satellites from ablated material alone may require a very large pebble reservoir. Directly captured planetesimals, despite contributing less total mass, can instead provide satellitesimals that grow through mutual collisions and serve as seeds for subsequent pebble accretion. Our results therefore favor a hybrid formation pathway in which the Galilean satellites grow through a combination of satellitesimal and pebble accretion. We further demonstrate that even a planetesimal reservoir containing less solid material than the minimum-mass solar nebula can supply sufficient building blocks to form the Galilean satellites. The balance between the ablation and direct capture depends sensitively on the efficiency of aerodynamic heating: if ablation is weaker than commonly assumed, direct capture can become the dominant source of satellite building blocks. These results connect the formation of Jupiter and its satellites by showing how Jupiter's growth regulates both the duration and form of solid delivery to its CPD.

papers.title: La Silla-QUEST RR Lyrae Survey III: The Shape of the Outer Virgo Overdensity
papers.micro: The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and 1 σ dispersion of 0.32…
papers.abstract: Using the La Silla-QUEST and Gaia surveys, we identify 256 RR Lyrae stars (RRLS) in the Outer Virgo Overdensity (OVOD). These show that the OVOD has a signifcantly larger and more complex shape than previously recognized. The OVOD lies at an average distance of ∼ 85 kpc, has a long dimension of ∼ 57° (∼ 85 kpc), and a width that varies from ∼ 10° (∼ 15 kpc) to ∼ 35° (∼ 50 kpc) in a prominent bulge. Because it bends by ∼ 35° from a great circle, it does not appear to be a stellar stream. The type ab RRLS (RRab) span a large range in period, with a mean of 0.59 days, and only 19± 3 % lie near the locus of Oosterhoff II variables in the Bailey diagram. The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and 1 σ dispersion of 0.32, as inferred from the RRab periods, suggest that the OVOD progenitor was a large dwarf galaxy. The hypothesis that the OVOD may be a shell produced by the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger citepchandra2023 is supported by the ∼ 70° angle that the southern extension of the OVOD makes with the orbits of red giants in its central part. The complex shape of the overall RRLS distribution, including a small north-south distance gradient, may also indicate, however, that we are seeing a blended, composite structure projected on the sky.

papers.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
papers.micro: Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near)a compact object…
papers.abstract: We develop a gauge-independent theory of magnetic reconnection beyond the standard special-relativistic framework of inertial systems in flat spacetime. Our definitions of reconnection and its rate are independent of reference frame and coordinate system, allowing physical effects of gravity and net linear acceleration to be distinguished from coordinate effects. We extend the mesoscale theory of Liu et al. [PRL 118, 085101 (2017)], in which the reconnection rate depends on physics both within the diffusion region and in an upstream ideal, force-free region. The theory identifies three non-inertial and curved-spacetime (NICS) effects, including gravitationally induced magnetic tension: gravitational distortion of the reconnection plane changes the curvature of magnetic field lines. Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near)a compact object, we find that (1) whether gravity increases or decreases the reconnection rate depends on the system's orientation relative to the gravitational source, with the greatest increase occurring when the outflow jet points toward or away from the source; and (2) the magnitude of the gravitational effect scales with the dimensionless parameter κ ≡ rsΔy²/r³, where r is the Schwarzschild radial coordinate, rs is the source's Schwarzschild radius, and Δy is the mesoscale length.

papers.title: VIDE 2.0: Robust, Scalable Void Finding for Extremely Large Galaxy Surveys
papers.micro: To answer the computational challenges posed by these surveys, in this paper we present VIDE 2.0, a significantly improved and enhanced void finding algorithm and analysis pipeline based on VIDE.
papers.abstract: Current and future spectroscopic and photometric galaxy surveys will deliver unprecedented numbers of galaxies, with expected counts in the tens of millions. To answer the computational challenges posed by these surveys, in this paper we present VIDE 2.0, a significantly improved and enhanced void finding algorithm and analysis pipeline based on VIDE. Leveraging the parameter-free identification of voids via a Voronoi tessellation and watershed scheme, we implement a robust mechanism for handling survey boundaries and incompleteness without relying on vast numbers of boundary particles. This new method identifies edge galaxies and flags voids contaminated by their presence. The mechanism is fully deterministic, producing bit-for-bit reproducible catalogs from identical inputs. An automatic rule for setting the mask resolution renders the entire pipeline parameter-free. Combined with other performance enhancements to the underlying VIDE engine, we find significant (>100×) speedups and a dramatic reduction in memory usage compared to previous versions: a 12-million-galaxy DESI Y1-class mock catalog now completes in roughly 15 minutes on a single laptop, where VIDE 1.0 could not run a catalog of even 10⁶ galaxies on the same hardware. We are also able to identify voids existing closer to survey boundaries via deterministic per-void contamination flags, maximizing their statistical potential. We exercise the upgraded pipeline on two large mock suites (MultiDark-Patchy DR12 and AbacusSummit DESI Y1 ELG), demonstrating converged cosmic-variance covariances for the void number function, the void-galaxy cross-correlation, and the void ellipticity distribution – key ingredients for Stage IV void cosmology. VIDE 2.0 is now well suited to handle large numbers of galaxies in mock and real observations, and ready to tackle the challenges of future campaigns.

papers.title: Turbulence Properties of Corotating Interaction Regions at 1 AU: a Comprehensive Superposed Epoch Analysis
papers.micro: Our findings offer valuable clues for reconciling discrepancies among earlier observational and simulation studies, and provide new insight into how compression and velocity shear modulate solar wind turbulence near CIRs.
papers.abstract: We perform a comprehensive superposed epoch analysis (SEA) of more than 200 corotating interaction regions (CIRs) using WIND spacecraft observations at 1 AU. The stream interfaces are identified by Minimum Variance Analysis (MVA), and turbulence properties are evaluated using wavelet transforms over a wide range of temporal scales. The analysis of normalized cross helicity (σc) and normalized residual energy (σr) reveals distinct turbulence behaviors across frequencies. The spectral indices of both magnetic and velocity fluctuations smoothly transition from steeper in the slow wind to shallower in the fast wind, while a localized steepening of the velocity spectra near the interface indicates enhanced dissipation due to compression. Across broad frequency bands, σc shows a clear dip at the stream interface, signifying increased inward Alfvén wave energy, whereas σr displays a peak-valley-peak structure mainly driven by large-scale velocity shear. In lower-frequency ranges, velocity shear artificially enhances velocity fluctuation energy, producing strong peaks in σr, while higher-frequency ranges show a smooth increase of σr from slow wind to fast wind. Nearly half of the analyzed CIRs are accompanied by a heliospheric current sheet (HCS), with many HCSs closely aligned with the stream interface, suggesting an intrinsic link between the two structures. Our findings offer valuable clues for reconciling discrepancies among earlier observational and simulation studies, and provide new insight into how compression and velocity shear modulate solar wind turbulence near CIRs.

papers.title: Accurate calibration method of the Back-linked Fabry Perot interferometer using null channel for space-based gravitational wave antenna
papers.micro: The results show that the residual laser frequency noise after calibration is more than an order of magnitude below the designed BLFPI sensitivity throughout the observation band.
papers.abstract: Accurate calibration of the detector response is essential for precision gravitational-wave (GW) observations. In the Back-linked Fabry-Perot Interferometer (BLFPI), which employs Fabry-Perot cavities to achieve high GW sensitivity, accurate calibration of the cavity response is particularly important because residual calibration errors directly limit the suppression of laser frequency noise. However, no practical calibration strategy for the cavity response has yet been established. In this paper, we propose a method for calibrating the cavity response using a null channel constructed from the three interferometer outputs of the triangular laser-link configuration. In null channel, GW signals are canceled and residual laser frequency noise indicates errors in the cavity response estimates. Therefore we can estimate the cavity response by optimizing the response parameters to minimize the integrated power of the null channel. We derive the estimation bias introduced by technical noise analytically and evaluate the performance of the proposed method numerically. The results show that the residual laser frequency noise after calibration is more than an order of magnitude below the designed BLFPI sensitivity throughout the observation band. This demonstrates that the proposed null-channel calibration method achieves the accuracy required for effective subtraction of laser frequency noise.

papers.title: Self-interacting Dark Matter signatures from stars extremely magnified by galaxy clusters
papers.micro: The observed lensed star distribution in the Dragon galaxy can be well explained…
papers.abstract: The spatial distribution of cluster-lensed star transients with respect to the macroscopic critical curve (CC) is sensitive to underlying substructures predicted by different classes of dark matter (DM) models. citetBroadhurst_2025 have shown that wave-like DM composed of ultra-light bosons better explains both the width and negative skewness (towards the interior of the CC) of the lensed star spatial distribution discovered in the “Dragon” lensed galaxy (z = 0.73) in the Abell 370 (A370, z = 0.375) cluster field, compared with the case of regular cold dark matter (CDM) subhaloes. In this work, we consider the case of self-interacting DM (SIDM) and investigate how the lensed star spatial distribution depends on the velocity-dependent self-interaction cross-section of SIDM particles, and whether constraints can be placed on the cross-section strength at relevant velocities. Establishing a cross-section strength-dependent (sub)halo gravothermal core-collapse probability, we found that the SIDM appears to be the only known class of models thus far in which the sign of skewness is set by its own particle parameters. The observed lensed star distribution in the Dragon galaxy can be well explained, in terms of both skewness and width, when a significant fraction of subhaloes have undergone core collapse and exhibit a steep power-law density slope. Given the cluster redshift, this qualitatively favours an (effective) cross-section strength of 500 −1000 cm²/g for halos with mass 10⁶ − 10⁸ M☉ (velocity dispersion of ∼ 1−10 km/s), when the role of environmental effects on the core-collapse (de)acceleration is not considered, and limits the three-dimensional inner density slope of the collapsed halo to Γ≳ 2.5 (Bayes factor of ∼ 10²).

papers.title: A Taxonomic Characterization of Targets in the Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt
papers.micro: We identify the remaining targets to be S-/L-, X-/C-, and D-types.
papers.abstract: The Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA) will investigate seven main-belt objects to improve our understanding of the distribution and evolution of water and metal-rich materials within the asteroid population. Understanding asteroid properties prior to the mission helps anticipate potential surface activity or hazards and optimize data acquisition during brief flyby windows, while also providing essential context for interpreting in-situ measurements within the broader asteroid population. We present visible-wavelength spectra (0.40-0.95 um) and corresponding taxonomic classifications for all seven EMA targets using Chi2 comparison with the visible portion of the Bus-DeMeo class templates. Notably, our analysis identifies two B-type asteroids, a relatively rare class, providing opportunities for future compositional comparisons between EMA targets and OSIRIS-REx observations of the organic-rich asteroid Bennu. We identify the remaining targets to be S-/L-, X-/C-, and D-types. The suite of asteroids selected for EMA offers a unique opportunity to investigate both intra-class variability and compositional differences across multiple taxonomic types, advancing our understanding of chemical and mineralogical heterogeneity in the asteroid belt.

papers.title: Earth accreted increasingly oxidized material as it grew constraining Theia to be small and relatively oxidized
papers.micro: A strong oxidizing gradient among the initial solids of the protoplanetary disk is favored to reproduce the chemistry of Earth's mantle, in agreement with Rubie et al. (2015b).
papers.abstract: Many different Solar System formation scenarios successfully reproduce the main astrophysical properties of the inner Solar System. Here, we use the chemistry of Earth's mantle to determine whether proposed Solar System formation scenarios can produce Earth and to constrain the characteristics of both the Proto-Earth and the Moon-forming impactor, Theia. To do this, we use a coupled N-body accretion and core-mantle differentiation model (Rubie et al., 2011, 2015b) applied to a range of proposed formation scenarios (Classical, Annulus, and Grand Tack scenarios). This model calculates the mantle chemistry of Earth-like planets in Solar System formation simulations and adjusts the initial redox state of the building blocks in a synthetic protoplanetary disk until the mantle of the simulated Earth closely matches the bulk silicate Earth. We find that a strong oxidizing gradient among the initial solids of the protoplanetary disk is favored to reproduce the chemistry of Earth's mantle, in agreement with Rubie et al. (2015b). The Solar System formation scenarios examined here successfully reproduce the composition of Earth if two related conditions are met: 1) there is a strong positive oxidation gradient with distance in the inner protoplanetary disk and 2) Earth accretes increasingly more oxidized material (on average) as it grows. Furthermore, in simulations that successfully reproduce Earth's composition, Proto-Earth and Theia may possess a wide range of mantle compositions and mass ratios. However, because late accretion is oxidizing across all proposed Solar System formation scenarios, Theia and Proto-Earth cannot both possess mantles that are more oxidized than the present-day Earth's mantle. Similarly, Theia's mantle may be significantly more oxidized than present-day Earth's mantle, but only if it is relatively small compared to the Proto-Earth.

papers.title: How Intensity Threshold Shapes the Velocity Dispersion-Size Relation in Molecular Clouds
papers.micro: Using 4916 ¹³CO clouds identified with GDCluster (Liu & Du 2025) in the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting (MWISP) survey…
papers.abstract: The velocity dispersion-size relation of molecular clouds, σv = C (R/1  pc)^γ, has been reported with a power-law index ranging from γ≈ 0.38 to 0.5 or higher, and a correspondingly varying normalization coefficient C, but the role of the intensity threshold in producing this scatter has not been quantitatively characterized. Using 4916 ¹³CO clouds identified with GDCluster (Liu & Du 2025) in the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting (MWISP) survey, we derive γ and C as functions of the intensity threshold Tth. The index γ increases monotonically with threshold, reaching a saturation value γsat ≈ 0.56 for the full sample; splitting the sample by spiral arm gives higher values, γsat ≈ 0.62 and 0.70. The normalization C(Tth) declines monotonically, saturating at Csat ≈ 0.35 km/s and implying a surface density of  46 Msun/pc^2 under a virial approximation. On the γ(Tth) curve, γ≈ 0.38 (Larson 1981) and γ≈ 0.5 (Solomon et al. 1987) correspond to a low threshold (Tth ≈ 1.2 K) and a near-saturation one (2.6 K), respectively, roughly consistent with the ¹³CO-equivalent boundary temperatures of these two studies. These two historically debated values, together with the broader γ≈ 0.38-0.7 range reported in the literature, may largely reflect different positions along this single threshold-dependent curve and differences in sample composition. This threshold effect should therefore be considered when using Larson-type relations to assess the roles of turbulence and gravity. As an independent check, DBSCAN-identified ¹³CO and ¹²CO samples show the same monotonic trend in γ, though the curve shape differs quantitatively.

papers.title: Influence of Alfven wave turbulence dissipation in stellar winds of the Sun and M dwarfs
papers.micro: These results suggest that the effects of chromospheric turbulence play a crucial role in modeling M-dwarf winds.
papers.abstract: The physics of M-dwarf stellar winds is increasingly being investigated within the framework of wave-driven models. In the case of the solar wind, Alfven-wave turbulence (AWT) is believed to play a crucial role in heating and accelerating the plasma. In this study, we perform one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations of the solar and M-dwarf winds using a model that incorporates shock heating generated by mode conversion and treats AWT as an optional component. For the solar wind, we confirm that including AWT reproduces the observed predominance of outwardly propagating Alfven waves, supporting the role of turbulent dissipation in driving the wind. We further validate this AWT-driven solar wind directly against Parker Solar Probe observations, finding good agreement in both the location of the Alfven point and the level of the normalized cross helicity in the fast solar wind. In M-dwarf simulations, we find that AWT dominates the overall heating budget within the investigated parameter range. A parameter survey of coronal magnetic field strength reveals that the dependence of the mass-loss rate on Bcor differs qualitatively between cases with and without AWT, highlighting the importance of chromospheric dissipation. In the absence of AWT, the resulting mass-loss rates are broadly consistent with previous studies and observations. In contrast, when AWT is included, the mass-loss rate is significantly reduced because turbulent dissipation decreases the Alfven-wave (Poynting) flux entering the corona. These results suggest that the effects of chromospheric turbulence play a crucial role in modeling M-dwarf winds.

papers.title: A faint thermonuclear X-ray burst from SAX J1808.4–3658 observed with NICER: possible evidence for burst-driven changes in the inner disk structure
papers.micro: At the peak of the burst, the neutron star's surface emission was fully exposed, subsequently becoming increasingly obscured while remaining above the pre-burst emission.
papers.abstract: We present spectral and temporal properties of a faint thermonuclear X-ray burst observed from SAX J1808.4–3658 by NICER. Unlike the previous analysis of the same burst citep2023ApJ...948..117C, our analysis focuses on the persistent spectral evolution and changes in the accretion environment. Following a peak flux of approximately 5% of the Eddington limit, the burst emission settled into a stable state characterized by a temperature of 0.46 keV and a flux 14% greater than the pre-burst value in the tail. Although the observation was truncated, it resumed after 3 hours, revealing that the source flux returned to its pre-burst level. Our spectral fitting results indicate that at the peak of the burst, the neutron star's surface emission was fully exposed, subsequently becoming increasingly obscured while remaining above the pre-burst emission. Fitting the persistent spectra also reveals an increase in the visible fraction of the neutron star's surface from 25% to 41% during the period from 100 s to 550 s after the burst, suggesting a change in the disk structure (the height or the inner radius). The spectral evolution suggests a transient reorganization of the inner accretion flow during the burst peak, followed by partial recovery as the burst flux declines.

papers.abstract: The non-detection of neutrinos associated with gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) has placed significant constraints on the physical parameter space of GRB jet models. However, most of these constraints have been derived using the time-integrated spectra. In this paper, we adopt time-resolved spectra, which provide a more detailed description of the prompt emission spectral structure, to calculate the neutrino emission, and investigate how they affect the constraints on GRB physical parameters. By selecting three GRBs (i.e., GRBs 090902B, 110721A and 080916C) whose spectra are composed of different components (e.g., thermal, thermal + non-thermal, and non-thermal), we find that the expected neutrino event numbers from the summed time-resolved spectra are lower than those from the time-integrated approach in the region of relatively low dissipation radius R and bulk Lorentz factor Γ, while the opposite trend is found at high R and high Γ. Moreover, we also use GECAM-C data to calculate the neutrino emission of the brightest GRB 221009A, and find that the expected number of neutrino events calculated from the summed time-resolved spectra is approximately three times that from the time-integrated spectra in the high-R and high-Γ regime. More details of constraints on the physical parameters are also discussed. These results highlight the importance of time-resolved spectra for future GRB neutrino studies.

papers.title: Sky Monitor AI: classifying night-sky conditions from an observatory all-sky camera with a CNN ensemble, label-free sky types and exact evidence maps
papers.micro: We release Sky Monitor AI, an open-source application for single frames, whole nights and live cameras.
papers.abstract: Small and remotely operated observatories must decide every night whether the sky is clear enough to observe. We classify frames of the auxiliary all-sky camera of the Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory as clear or cloudy, using 8806 frames from 32 nights. A circular sky mask removes a printed date stamp that would act as a shortcut, and all evaluations use whole held-out nights. On six test nights, hand-crafted sky statistics reach 77.1% accuracy, a small CNN trained from scratch 84.3%, and a validation-selected ensemble of the small CNN and two ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 variants 86.7% (AUC 0.924) with the smallest night-to-night scatter. Moonlight is the dominant difficulty: across Moon altitude the ensemble's accuracy varies by 5 percentage points, the hand-crafted model's by 20. Fine-tuning deeper ResNet layers overfits with about 24 training nights, underlining the need to match model capacity to the number of independent nights. The labels were assigned in blocks of 1-2 h, and many remaining errors are mislabelled or partly cloudy frames. Without labels, clustering of pretrained CNN embeddings recovers the clear/cloudy split with 87% purity and isolates frames with water droplets on the camera dome. Gradient-based maps and a rim test indicate that the networks rely on sky regions. For networks ending in global average pooling, the decision decomposes exactly into local logits, giving gradient-free evidence maps and a cloud-cover estimate. We release Sky Monitor AI, an open-source application for single frames, whole nights and live cameras.

papers.title: A Failed Filament Eruption and Associated Active Region Heating Driven by External Magnetic Reconnection
papers.micro: These results suggest that the strong confining field halted the filament eruption and sustained the interface compression required for current sheet formation…
papers.abstract: We investigate a failed filament eruption and associated coronal heating in NOAA Active Region 12353 on 2015 May 23, focusing on the relationship between magnetic confinement and external reconnection. Coordinated observations from the Goode Solar Telescope and the Solar Dynamics Observatory, together with nonlinear force-free field extrapolations, allow us to trace the event from the merging of two low-lying filamentary structures to the failed eruption of the resulting elongated filament. Before the rapid rise, the modeled flux rope had entered a regime susceptible to kink instability, while low-atmospheric internal reconnection had already occurred; both may have contributed to the initial acceleration. The rising flux rope remained below the torus instability threshold and was confined by a strong, asymmetric overlying field that compressed it against the overlying loops. An elongated interface brightening, bidirectional plasmoid-like motions, newly brightened loop systems, and progressive weakening of the filament are consistent with external reconnection that changed the magnetic connectivity, removed magnetic flux from the rope, and disrupted its coherent structure. Differential emission measure analysis indicates that the external reconnection heated the active region loop system. A transient, localized structure with high-temperature emission was observed at the interaction interface, consistent with the expected location of a current sheet associated with external reconnection. These results suggest that the strong confining field halted the filament eruption and sustained the interface compression required for current sheet formation, enabling external reconnection to disrupt the flux rope and heat the active region loop system.
